pairs.evidence: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:238 The hook's reminder restates the Documentation Sync rule instead of citing it. Its copy has already lost the 'CLI-observable behavior' class that .claude/CLAUDE.md lists, so the agent is shown a narrower rule than the file states.

techniques.evidence: scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:238 The rule text is copied into the hook rather than pointed to, and the copy has already drifted from the canonical rule (it drops CLI-observable behavior).

scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:211 The hook moved to per-entry satisfaction (line 220), but .claude/CLAUDE.md:25 still tells agents it stays silent when 'the turn touched any docs/features/*'. That is a confident stale line about a gate.

scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:2 The checkable half of the doc-sync rule (mapped source edited, doc not edited) runs as a Stop hook. The judgment half (is the change user-visible?) stays in prose with a one-sentence dismiss path.
scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:261 Exit 3 sends instrument failures to the human rather than steering the model, because the model cannot fix them. Cannot-comply is kept apart from would-not-comply.

scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.test.mjs:241 The hook depends on the harness's transcript envelope, which is a harness default. A canary test checks it against real transcripts, so a harness change fails a test instead of silencing the hook.
